name: Manual-Free Gaze Selection
summary: Gaze points at objects, and a model reading only the eye-movement data decides when the user means to select, so no button, pinch or dwell is needed.
howItWorks: Gaze features around each fixated object (fixation and saccade measures) are turned into log-likelihoods under a Bayesian framework, fitted per task context, and fed to a kernel SVM that predicts selection intention in real time. When the model predicts intent, the looked-at object is selected automatically. Models were trained on data from 20 participants and tested with 25 others on a Quest Pro in a word-category search task among distractors, against gaze pointing confirmed by controller trigger, by pinch, and by 600 ms dwell.
advantages: No hand or dwell action needed.
Avoids the fixed time cost of dwell.

relationships.note: Compared with gaze plus trigger and gaze plus dwell.
Also predicts selection intent from eye movements.
